title: Base Case, General Case, and Designing Recursion

blocks.value: Every recursive method needs a selection structure (if/else) that splits it into two kinds of cases: the base case, which stops the recursion directly without calling itself again, and the general case, which calls itself on a smaller version of the problem. Without a base case, a recursive method would call itself forever.

Steps for designing a recursive method:
1. Understand the problem requirements.
2. Determine the limiting conditions.
3. Identify the base case(s) and solve each directly.
4. Identify the general case(s) and solve each in terms of a smaller version of the same problem.
Example: finding the largest value in an array by recursively shrinking the range being searched.
